t: Model Loader - Signature build-tool concept
title: Model Loader - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Loads compatible model weights into an execution environment.
description:
Model Loader is the Signature build-tool concept that loads compatible model weights into an execution environment. In the Signature line, it is not a loose collection of scripts but a deterministic capability: the same build request produces the same verified result on every run, on every machine. This database documents the concept in full - what it is, the seven framework pillars that implement it, the real techniques it stands on, the standards it honors, and laddered drills that teach it from first principles to compounded mastery.

An AI that builds on demand needs Model Loader the way a workshop needs its central bench. Without it, every build becomes improvisation: requirements drift, steps run out of order, and nobody can say why a result came out the way it did. With it, the build becomes a protocol - inputs declared, transformations explicit, outputs checked against the original request. That protocol is what these records describe, pillar by pillar.

Every record in this database carries a runnable demonstration program, because a build tool that cannot show its work cannot be trusted with real work. Read the overview, study the pillars, practice the drills, and run the demos: by the end the Model Loader will be a capability you can invoke, not a concept you have read about.

t: Signature Loader - Model Loader framework pillar
title: Signature Loader - Model Loader framework pillar
definition: The Loader component of the Signature Model Loader framework, owning loader. Signature concept.
description:
The Loader is a load-bearing component of the Signature Model Loader framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's loader responsibilities belongs to the Loader, and the Loader answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Loader can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Loader works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Model Loader charter (loads compatible model weights into an execution environment.). The Loader reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for a small models job that needs Model Loader. The Loader takes the request's loader responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Loader's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Model Loader. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Quantizer - Model Loader framework pillar
title: Signature Quantizer - Model Loader framework pillar
definition: The Quantizer component of the Signature Model Loader framework, owning quantizer. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature Model Loader framework, the Quantizer owns the framework's quantizer responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Quantizer's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Quantizer from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. Every execution is checked against the charter (Loads compatible model weights into an execution environment.). If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Walk through it concretely. A AI model integration build needs Model Loader, so the framework invokes the Quantizer on the the framework's quantizer responsibilities portion of the work. The demo program attached to this record executes the pillar's essential algorithm on sample data - run it with node and watch each step print its reasoning. Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.

t: Signature Router - Model Loader framework pillar
title: Signature Router - Model Loader framework pillar
definition: The Router component of the Signature Model Loader framework, owning router. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Model Loader framework decomposes the capability (Loads compatible model weights into an execution environment.) into seven pillars, and the Router is the one that owns the framework's router responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Model Loader result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Router's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Router's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.
